name: Neo.mjs
description: The Neo.mjs Application Engine — a multi-threaded, JSON-first UI framework with an AI-native Agent OS. The system anchor for the entire concept ontology.

name: Multi-Threading Architecture
description: Neo.mjs distributes application logic across dedicated Web Workers (App, VDom, Data, Canvas, Task), keeping the main thread reserved exclusively for DOM updates. This is the platform's defining architectural decision.

name: Off-Main-Thread Execution
description: Application business logic runs inside a dedicated App Worker, not on the main thread. The main thread only receives minimal DOM-delta payloads, eliminating jank and enabling true parallelism.

name: Worker Isolation
description: Each worker type (App, VDom, Data, Canvas, Task) has a dedicated responsibility. App Workers run component logic; VDom Workers compute deltas; Data Workers handle network I/O; Canvas Workers handle OffscreenCanvas rendering.

name: SharedWorker Mode
description: Neo.mjs can run its worker infrastructure inside SharedWorkers, allowing multiple browser tabs or windows to share state, components, and communication channels — enabling true multi-window applications.

name: Cross-Thread Communication
description: Workers communicate via structured postMessage RPC calls. The framework provides a transparent promise-based API that makes cross-thread calls look like synchronous local calls, hiding the async boundary.

name: JSON-First VDOM Protocol
description: UI descriptions are plain JSON objects, not a compiled template language. Components define their VDOM as nested JSON structures, enabling programmatic manipulation, serialization, and cross-thread transfer without parsing.

name: VDOM as IPC Layer
description: The JSON-based virtual DOM doubles as the inter-process communication format between the App Worker and VDom Worker. State changes are expressed as VDOM mutations, serialized to postMessage, then delta-computed in the VDom Worker.

name: Delta Update Pipeline
description: The VDom Worker compares old and new VDOM trees, computes a minimal set of DOM operations (deltas), and sends only those operations to the main thread. This minimizes main-thread work and eliminates full re-renders.

name: Asymmetric VDOM Updates
description: Components can surgically update individual VDOM nodes without re-rendering the full tree. Using vdom path accessors, a single property change can target a specific nested element, enabling fine-grained reactivity.

name: Two-Tier Reactivity
description: Neo.mjs provides two complementary reactivity models: push-based reactivity via the Config System (explicit lifecycle hooks) and pull-based reactivity via Effects (automatic dependency tracking). Developers choose the right model for each use case.

name: Push-Based Reactivity (Config System)
description: Reactive properties defined with a trailing underscore (e.g., myConfig_) trigger explicit lifecycle hooks (beforeSet, afterSet, beforeGet) when changed. This is the primary reactivity model, providing full control over change propagation.

name: Reactive Configs (Trailing Underscore)
description: Properties declared with a trailing underscore in the static config block (e.g., text_: 'Hello') automatically generate getter/setter pairs with beforeSet/afterSet hooks. The underscore is a compile-time signal to Neo.setupClass().

name: Lifecycle Hooks (beforeSet / afterSet / beforeGet)
description: Reactive configs support three lifecycle hooks: beforeSet (validation/transformation), afterSet (side effects like VDOM updates), and beforeGet (lazy computation). The naming convention is method-level: beforeSetMyConfig(), afterSetMyConfig().

name: Config Descriptors & Merge Strategies
description: Configs can use descriptor objects with metadata controlling inheritance behavior. The 'merge' property supports 'shallow' and 'deep' strategies for hierarchical config merging across the prototype chain.

name: The undefined Sentinel Value
description: When a reactive config is set to the literal value undefined, Neo.mjs interprets this as 'do not apply this config'. This allows subclasses to selectively opt out of inherited default values without triggering afterSet hooks.

name: Pull-Based Reactivity (Effects)
description: Effect instances automatically track which reactive configs they read and re-execute when any dependency changes. This provides computed-property-like behavior without explicit dependency declarations.

name: Class System & Compilation
description: Neo.mjs enhances JavaScript classes with a reactive config system, automatic namespace registration, mixin support, and a prototype-chain-based inheritance model. All classes are processed via Neo.setupClass().

name: Neo.setupClass() (The Gatekeeper)
description: The central class registration function. It traverses the prototype chain, merges static configs from all ancestors, generates reactive getter/setter pairs, applies mixins, registers the class in the global namespace, and handles singleton instantiation.

name: Mixin Architecture
description: Neo.mjs supports multiple inheritance via mixins. Mixins are applied during setupClass(), copying methods and reactive configs from mixin prototypes to the target class. Conflict detection prevents silent overwrites.

name: Instance Lifecycle
description: The lifecycle of a Neo.mjs instance: construct() → config application → onConstructed() → initAsync() (if defined). The constructor phase is synchronous; initAsync() provides a hook for async initialization that runs after the instance is fully configured.

name: Zero-Build Development Mode
description: In development mode, Neo.mjs runs directly from native ES modules — no bundler, no transpiler, no build step. The browser imports source files directly. Production builds use webpack for optimization but are not required during development.

name: Multi-Window Applications
description: Neo.mjs natively supports applications that span multiple browser windows, sharing state, stores, and components across windows via SharedWorkers. Components can be moved between windows at runtime.

name: Object Permanence
description: Component instances persist in the App Worker's memory regardless of DOM visibility. Removing a component from a view does not destroy it — it can be re-inserted elsewhere, even in a different window, with its full state intact.

name: AI-Native Architecture (Agent OS)
description: Neo.mjs includes a full AI agent infrastructure: 4 MCP servers (Knowledge Base, Memory Core, GitHub Workflow, Neural Link), a Dream Pipeline for strategic forecasting, and a Swarm Intelligence delegation model. The framework is self-improving.

name: Neural Link (WebSocket Bridge)
description: A WebSocket-based MCP server that bridges LLM agents to live Neo.mjs applications. Agents can inspect component trees, modify state, simulate events, and hot-patch code at runtime — providing full-stack application mutability.

name: Knowledge Base (Semantic RAG)
description: An MCP server backed by ChromaDB that provides semantic search over the entire indexed codebase (source, guides, examples, tickets, releases). It performs ETL from source to JSONL to vector embeddings, with class-hierarchy boosting.

name: Memory Core (Episodic Memory)
description: An MCP server providing persistent episodic memory for AI agents. Stores raw agent interactions, generates session summaries, and maintains a Native Edge Graph (SQLite) for structural knowledge and Hebbian decay.

name: Dream Pipeline (REM / Sandman)
description: The DreamService processes undigested session memories through 6 phases: Workspace Ingestion, Tri-Vector Extraction, Topological Conflict Detection, Capability Gap Inference, Garbage Collection, and Golden Path Synthesis.

name: Swarm Intelligence
description: Multi-agent delegation model where an Orchestrator assigns tasks from the Golden Path to autonomous agents. Fat Tickets carry rich architectural context. Stigmergic coordination via the shared Native Edge Graph.

name: Golden Path Synthesis
description: A forecasting algorithm that combines semantic distance (ChromaDB vector proximity to the current work frontier) with structural weight (accumulated graph edge weights) to mathematically rank which tasks the swarm should work on next.

name: Component Architecture
description: Neo.mjs components are JSON-described UI building blocks managed by the App Worker. They support class-based and functional paradigms, reactive configs, container composition, and cross-thread rendering via the VDOM protocol.

name: Class-Based Components
description: Components defined as classes extending Neo.component.Base. They declare their UI via a static _vdom config, respond to state changes via lifecycle hooks, and can contain child components via the items config.

name: Functional Components
description: Lightweight components defined as functions that return VDOM JSON objects. They use Effects for reactivity instead of class-based lifecycle hooks, providing a simpler API for stateless or self-contained UI elements.

name: Component Composition (Containers & Items)
description: Containers (Neo.container.Base) hold child components in their items array. Composition replaces inheritance for building complex UIs — a Panel contains a Toolbar and a Body, rather than extending both.

name: Observable Mixin & Event System
description: The Observable mixin provides a DOM-style event system for non-DOM objects. Classes marked as static observable = true gain addListener/fireEvent/on APIs. Event delegation in the VDOM maps DOM events to component methods.

name: Data Layer
description: Neo.mjs provides Records, Stores, Collections, and State Providers for managing application data. Records use factory-based lazy instantiation. Stores handle filtering, sorting, and remote data loading. State Providers enable hierarchical shared state.

name: Records & RecordFactory
description: Data records are created via RecordFactory for lazy instantiation. Fields are defined with types and default values. Records track dirty state and can serialize to JSON for network transport.

name: Stores & Collections
description: Stores extend Collection to manage arrays of Records with built-in filtering, sorting, and grouping. Remote stores handle API communication. Collections provide a reactive, observable data container.

name: State Provider (Hierarchical State Management)
description: State Providers implement hierarchical shared state. Child components inherit and can bind to parent state. Changes propagate through the component tree. This replaces external state management libraries.

name: Data Pipelines
description: A declarative system for defining request/response transformation chains. Pipelines compose middleware-like stages for API communication, including serialization, authentication, error handling, and caching.

name: Layout System
description: Containers use layout managers to arrange child components. Built-in layouts include Base, Card, Flexbox (HBox, VBox), Grid (CSS Grid), Accordion, and Fit. Layouts are applied via the container's layout config.

name: Forms Engine
description: Neo.mjs supports true nested forms (impossible in native HTML), detached validation, and 20+ field types. Form containers can nest arbitrarily deep while maintaining a single validation context.

name: Theming Engine
description: Themes are built with SCSS and exposed via CSS custom properties. Components consume theme tokens rather than hard-coded values. The build system generates optimized theme maps. Dark mode and glassmorphism are first-class supported patterns.

name: Routing
description: URL hash-based routing maps URL patterns to application states. The HashHistory class parses hash fragments into key-value pairs that drive component visibility and tabbed navigation.

name: Drag and Drop
description: The DragZone and DropZone system provides configurable drag-and-drop with visual feedback, proxy elements, and cross-component data transfer. Works within the worker architecture via DOM event delegation.

name: Grid Component
description: A high-performance data grid supporting buffered rendering, virtual scrolling, column locking, cell editing, row selection, and multi-body architecture. Handles 50,000+ rows via viewport-aware rendering.

name: Canvas Architecture (Zero-Allocation)
description: OffscreenCanvas rendering runs in a dedicated Canvas Worker, achieving zero main-thread allocation for complex visualizations. The canvas uses a scene-graph model with JSON-described render instructions.

name: Build Architecture & Service Workers
description: Production builds use webpack to bundle, tree-shake, and optimize the application. Service Workers enable offline capability and caching. Four build environments are supported: development, dist/development, dist/production, and test.

name: 4 Environments
description: Neo.mjs supports four runtime environments: development (raw ES modules), dist/development (bundled, unminified), dist/production (bundled, minified, optimized), and a dedicated test environment for Playwright.

name: RPC Layer
description: A transparent promise-based Remote Procedure Call system that enables cross-worker method invocation. The App Worker can call methods on components in the VDom Worker as if they were local, with the framework handling serialization and routing.

name: Progressive Disclosure Skills
description: Agent skills are folder-based instruction sets (.agent/skills/) that extend agent capabilities. They follow a SKILL.md + references pattern, loading detailed instructions only when triggered — preventing context window bloat.

name: Native Edge Graph
description: A SQLite-backed knowledge graph maintained by the Memory Core. Stores typed nodes (CLASS, METHOD, FILE, ISSUE, CONCEPT) with weighted edges. Supports Hebbian decay, topological traversal, and orphan pruning.

name: VDOM Teleportation
description: Components can be moved between windows at runtime by serializing their VDOM JSON to a different browser context. The component's state persists in the App Worker — only the rendering target changes.

name: Focus Management
description: The FocusManager tracks focus across the component tree, providing keyboard navigation, focus trapping for dialogs, and cross-component focus coordination — all managed from the App Worker.

name: Streaming Data & Progressive Rendering
description: Stores can incrementally receive and render data as it arrives from streaming APIs. Combined with buffered grid rendering, this enables real-time data visualization without blocking the UI.

name: TreeStore & Hierarchical Data
description: A specialized store for tree-structured data. Manages parent-child relationships, expansion state, and lazy loading of child nodes. Powers TreeList and other hierarchical components.

name: Declarative Component Trees vs Imperative VDOM
description: Neo.mjs supports two VDOM authoring modes: declarative (nested component items arrays) and imperative (direct VDOM JSON manipulation). Declarative is preferred for composition; imperative is used for fine-grained control.

name: Config System Deep Dive
description: The complete config inheritance system: static class-level configs, prototype chain merging, descriptor-based merge strategies, the configSymbol holding zone during construction, and the relationship between class configs and instance configs.
